title: Sasikumar’s ‘Vadhandhi’ Season 2 Sets August Premiere on Prime Video (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Prime Video will globally premiere “Vadhandhi – The Mystery of Mani” this August, the streamer revealed, bringing back its Tamil-language original s
body:
Prime Video will globally premiere “Vadhandhi – The Mystery of Mani” this August, the streamer revealed, bringing back its Tamil-language original suspense thriller franchise for a second season.

	Andrew Louis, who created and wrote the first season, returns to write and direct Season 2, with Pushkar and Gayatri overseeing the project as creative producers under their Wallwatcher Films banner. Across eight episodes, M. Sasikumar plays SI Moosa Raza, a lawman whose search for answers puts him at odds with political pressure, press attention and his own weaknesses. Yashwanth, Anagha Maruthora, Aparna Das, Vivek Prasanna, Revathy Sharma and Arjun Nandhakumar round out the cast in pivotal roles.
	

	Set in Madurai, the season weaves its investigation narrative through the culturally rich backdrop of the Jallikattu festival, continuing the franchise’s throughline of rumor versus reality. The case begins when skeletal remains surface during ceremonies marking the launch of a highway project, a discovery that puts Moosa Raza on the trail of an elusive prisoner named Mani.


	The series will stream on Prime Video in Tamil, with dubs in Telugu and Hindi and subtitles in 15 languages including English, worldwide from Aug. 7. 

	“Stories from the South have received immense love and appreciation from audiences across the world, and ‘Vadhandhi’ is a franchise we are incredibly proud of. The first season carved a unique space in the suspense crime drama genre by masterfully blurring the lines between rumor and reality, and we are thrilled to bring the second season to audiences worldwide. With Andrew Louis at the helm once again, and a gripping narrative set against the vibrant cultural landscape of Madurai, season 2 takes the franchise to new heights. It is a privilege to continue our collaboration with Pushkar and Gayatri, whose ability to craft compelling, culturally rooted stories with universal appeal is unmatched. We are confident this season will keep audiences on the edge of their seats,” said Nikhil Madhok, director and head of originals, Prime Video India.
	

	Wallwatcher Films, founded by Pushkar and Gayatri, previously produced both seasons of “Suzhal – The Vortex,” the franchise’s first season, “Vadhandhi – The Fable of Velonie,” and the series “Exam” for Prime Video, along with the short “The Mask” and the Netflix feature “Aelay.”

	“Season 2 builds on the franchise’s unique blend of suspense, truth and perception while telling a story that is both emotionally compelling and deeply engaging. Andrew Louis has yet again brought this vision to life brilliantly, crafting a gripping narrative that stays true to the spirit of the franchise while taking it in an exciting new direction. Sasikumar and the entire cast have delivered exceptional performances that add tremendous depth to the story,” said Pushkar and Gayatri, creative producers on the series.

	Prime Video is home to Tamil-language titles alongside a wider slate that includes “Mirzapur,” “The Family Man,” “Panchayat” and “Paatal Lok,” as well as global series including “The Boys” and “The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power.”

schema.headline: Sasikumar’s ‘Vadhandhi’ Season 2 Sets August Premiere on Prime Video (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Bill Oddie, Wildlife Presenter and Comedian, Dies at 85
description:
Bill Oddie, the English comedian and conservationist known for hosting wildlife programs including BBC’s “Springwatch,” has died. He was 85.

	Oddie
body:
Bill Oddie, the English comedian and conservationist known for hosting wildlife programs including BBC’s “Springwatch,” has died. He was 85.

	Oddie’s agent, David Foster, confirmed his death in a statement to BBC News on Monday, calling him “the country’s best-loved birder.”

	Foster continued: “Bill was a multi-talented celebrity — wildlife presenter, broadcaster, comedian, writer, songwriter, musician and conservationist. Yet it was never fame that he valued. Instead he encouraged us to respect and protect the environment. He taught us the wonder of it. He protested, lobbied and campaigned for it. He led the way and people of all ages and backgrounds responded to his call. And such a massive contribution to conservation will never be forgotten.”
	

	Oddie got his start on the TV comedy series “The Goodies” alongside his Cambridge classmates Tim Brooke-Taylor and Graeme Garden, which ran from 1970 to 1982. He then shifted to presenting and focused on his love of wildlife, specifically birds. He hosted a slew of successful nature programs for the BBC from the mid-80s to 2008, including “Birding With Bill Oddie,” “Bill Oddie Goes Wild,” “Springwatch,” “Autumnwatch” and more.


	Born on July 7, 1941, in Rochdale, Lancashire, England, Oddie moved to Birmingham at a young age and was raised by his father and grandmother. He went on to study English literature at Cambridge University, and it was there that he became interested in comedy, appearing in several productions of the sketch comedy troupe Footlights. 

	In the late ’60s, he began his venture into show business as a key member of the BBC radio program “I’m Sorry, I’ll Read That Again,” on which several of his musical compositions were featured. After writing and performing on comedy series including “Twice a Fortnight” and “Broaden Your Mind,” Oddie got his big break with “The Goodies,” known for its surreal sketches and situational comedy. In addition to writing and acting on the series, Oddie wrote all the music including co-penning the show’s theme song.
	

	In the mid-’80s, Oddie became increasingly interested in wildlife, drawing from his lifelong passion of birdwatching. This kickstarted the second phase of his career, in which he became a beloved nature presenter known for programs including “Oddie in Paradise” (1985), “Birding With Bill Oddie” (1997-1998, 2000), “Bill Oddie Goes Wild” (2001-2003), “Bill Oddie’s How to Watch Wildlife” (2005-2006), “Springwatch” (2005-2008), “Autumnwatch” (2006-2008) and “Bill Oddie’s Wild Side” (2008).

	In 2003, he was made an OBE for his services to wildlife conservation.

	Oddie is survived by his wife Laura and daughters Bonnie, Kate and Rosie.

schema.headline: Bill Oddie, Wildlife Presenter and Comedian, Dies at 85

title: Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong Urge U.K. Government to Block Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger in Op-Ed: ‘It Threatens to Inflict Immense Harm’
description: Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong have urged the U.K. government to intervene in the proposed Paramount-Warner Bros merger, sayin
body:
Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong have urged the U.K. government to intervene in the proposed Paramount-Warner Bros merger, saying it “threatens to inflict immense harm on the British public.”

	In an op-ed addressed to culture minister Lisa Nandy, the trio said her intervention could be “prove one of the most important decisions any culture secretary has taken for UK film, television and media in a generation.”
	

	They argue that the merger will result in “redundancies, cancelled productions, fewer films commissioned and fewer risks taken,” although they acknowledge that aspect of the merger is less within Nandy’s remit than the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), which is also reviewing the deal. Nandy’s is to decide whether the merger is in the public interest, to which Cumberbatch, Cumming and Wong say “It most certainly is not.” The trio point to the fact that Paramount currently owns public service broadcaster Channel 5 as well as CBS in the States: the acquisition of WBD would see CNN and CNN International also come under the same umbrella.


	“If one commercially interested owner controls access to both [the CNN and CBS news archives], they control the raw material of our historical memory,” the op-ed, published in the Guardian, states.

	“Nandy has opened the door to intervention. She must walk through it, for the sake of everyone who makes U.K. television and film – and everyone who watches it. If she does not, we will be left without the ability to protect our industry and our culture from this consolidation. We must not push the public’s interest aside; we must stand up for it and block this merger.”
	

	Nandy has already said she is “minded to intervene” in the deal, although Parliament is now in recess until Sept. 1. The culture secretary, who managed to cling on to her job in the wake of a cabinet reshuffle by incoming Prime Minister Andy Burnham, currently has a number of high-profile media matters to attend to, including the equally if not more impactful acquisition of ITV by Comcast-owned Sky as well as the BBC’s royal charter renewal. 

	Last week the European Commission approved the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger, albeit with some conditions.

	In the U.S., however, it is facing opposition from numerous sources. As of Friday, Paramount agreed to postpone the merger until after an antitrust trial.

schema.headline: Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong Urge U.K. Government to Block Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger in Op-Ed: ‘It Threatens to Inflict Immense Harm’

title: ‘The Legend of Kitchen Soldier,’ ‘Yumi’s Cells’ Lead Prime Video India’s Slate of 100-Plus New CJ ENM Titles
description: Prime Video India and Korean powerhouse CJ ENM have signed a multi-year distribution deal that will add more than 100 Korean titles to the streamer’
body:
Prime Video India and Korean powerhouse CJ ENM have signed a multi-year distribution deal that will add more than 100 Korean titles to the streamer’s Indian lineup over the next two years.

	The agreement covers 26 new titles from CJ ENM alongside a broader slate drawn from the studio’s existing library, and extends the companies’ existing global partnership with a dedicated focus on India. New and upcoming titles under the deal will carry English subtitles and dubbing in the Hindi, Tamil and Telugu languages.
	

	The slate opens with “Yumi’s Cells” Season 3, the latest chapter of CJ ENM’s flagship franchise, which topped streaming charts in 81 countries, including the U.S., Brazil, France and the U.A.E. Also on the schedule are “Filing for Love,” which ranked No. 1 in 105 countries; breakout series “The Legend of Kitchen Soldier“; and romantic comedy “My Bias, My Boss.” The deal also folds in library titles such as “Dear X,” “Law in the City,” “Study Group,” “My Dearest Nemesis,” “Search: WWW” and the first two seasons of “Yumi’s Cells.” The lineup features talent including Kim You-Jung, Lee Jong-suk, Park Ji-hoon and Cha Woo-min, spanning drama, thriller, romance, fantasy and action genres.


	“Building on our strong global relationship with CJ ENM and the deal announced last year, we’re excited to deepen this collaboration with a sharper focus on India,” said Shilangi Mukherji, director and head, SVOD business, Prime Video India. “The popularity of Korean content has been remarkable across our Prime Video markets. Compelling narratives, diverse genres, and memorable characters that transcend borders have fueled a K-content wave that continues to gain momentum year on year. By bringing a curated slate of premium Korean titles to Prime Video, we’re doubling down on our commitment to making the most innovative and captivating stories from Korea accessible to audiences in India.”
	

	The India-focused pact builds on a run of recent moves by CJ ENM to widen its footprint in the country. The studio and Prime Video first struck a multi-year global distribution deal in May 2025 at the WAVES Bazaar market in Mumbai, which gave the streamer worldwide rights, excluding Korea and China, to CJ ENM titles including “Head Over Heels.” CJ ENM followed that in September 2025 with a separate licensing deal bringing 18 K-dramas to Amazon’s free, ad-supported MX Player service in India.

	“We are pleased to collaborate with Prime Video India to bring CJ ENM’s acclaimed K-dramas to a wider audience in one of the world’s most dynamic entertainment markets,” said Seo Jangho, executive VP of platform division at CJ ENM. “Prime Video’s unmatched reach in India, combined with its deep investment in local audiences, makes it the ideal partner to amplify our content to millions of new viewers. This partnership reflects our ongoing commitment to expanding the global reach of Korean storytelling. We look forward to connecting more deeply with Indian audiences and sharing the richness and emotional depth of K-dramas with viewers across the region.”

	Prime members will be able to stream the new titles at no additional cost.

	“At Prime Video India, we keep a keen eye on what our customers are watching and what stories resonate with them,” said Manish Menghani, director and head of content licensing, Prime Video, India. “The surge in popularity of K-content is undeniable. CJ ENM is one of the biggest entertainment studios in Korea, with an expansive library of much-loved titles such as ‘Legend of the Blue Sea,’ ‘Prison Playbook,’ ‘Mother,’ and ‘A Practical Guide to Love,’ among several others – all of which will be launching on Prime Video over the next two years. The continued success of our global content deal with CJ ENM is a testament to this growing demand. For us, this deal is not only the natural step forward, backed by customer preferences, but also a reflection of commitment to making Prime Video India the go-to destination for the best international content.”

schema.headline: ‘The Legend of Kitchen Soldier,’ ‘Yumi’s Cells’ Lead Prime Video India’s Slate of 100-Plus New CJ ENM Titles

title: Dylan Mulvaney Fires Back After Trump Mocks Her and Kaitlan Collins in White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech: ‘Actually the Greatest Compliment of All’
description: Dylan Mulvaney has hit back at U.S. President Donald Trump after he mocked the trans advocate, actress and singer in his White House Correspondents’
body:
Dylan Mulvaney has hit back at U.S. President Donald Trump after he mocked the trans advocate, actress and singer in his White House Correspondents’ Dinner speech on Friday.

	“My name is Dylan Mulvaney and the president said my name four times in his speech on Friday night,” she began a TikTok video response posted on Sunday evening.  

	At Friday’s rescheduled dinner, which had been postponed after a gunman opened fire at the original event in April, Trump mentioned Mulvaney after CNN’s Kaitlan Collins accepted an award for her covering the White House. Trump compared the two women and brought up the 2023 Bud Light controversy, where customers boycotted the beer brand after Mulvaney posted a social media ad featuring her face on a can. 
	

	“I thought Kaitlan had really made it big with a major new sponsorship, but then I informed her that it wasn’t her on the Bud Light can, it was Dylan Mulvaney,” Trump said in his speech. “Dylan Mulvaney cost Bud Light $35 billion in market cap. That was the worst commercial ever made by the way, for those few people who want to hear that. Most people don’t care, but I would. I wouldn’t want to hire Dylan any time soon.”


	In her response, Mulvaney — who most recently starred in the Broadway musical “Six” — first congratulated Collins, saying: “I’m incredibly honored to be compared to her in any way and I hope that she continues doing all the great work.” She then marveled at the fact that she’s “been kind of flying under the radar” since the Bud Light video, but is “still his topic of conversation all these years later.”
	

	“It seems to me that I might be the one that got away for these men, like I am permanently burned into their retinas, I am microchipped into their minds,” Mulvaney said, adding that perhaps “being publicly mocked and criticized by this administration is actually, like, the greatest compliment of all because it puts me in the company of some of the most brilliant, empathetic people in our world today.”

	Since his speech on Friday night, Trump has doubled down on his comments about Collins and Mulvaney, posting an AI-generated photo from the beer ad placing Collins’ face on Mulvaney’s body.

	“But I do still wonder, why is it so important to them that I don’t find success? What is it that I have that they don’t?” Mulvaney asked. “Oh my God… freedom! I am free in a way that they will never have the privilege to experience, and they want to use their power to take away my freedom. But what they don’t understand is my freedom has zero contingency on what they can provide for me, because my freedom is fully dependent on the moment that I acknowledged my real, authentic self, and every day since. And sharing that with the world, it’s just icing on the cake. But they don’t want me to be able to share that, because it would mean young people realizing that if someone like me can be themselves and find success and freedom, then they can find success and freedom for themselves, too.”

	Mulvaney then gave her viewers some “action items,” emphasizing that it is more important than ever to support trans and nonbinary people, especially young people seeking acceptance. 

	“When they try to judge you for your support of us, take that as the greatest compliment,” she said. “Ladies, when they tell you that you look like a trans woman, wear it like a medal. Men, when they tell you that being attracted to trans women makes you gay, I want you to Hilary Duff PSA their ass so hard that they don’t even know what just happened. And to the dolls, let’s have each other’s back.”

	She concluded her video response with a message directly to Trump, saying: “To the president, thank you for reminding me that I am more powerful than I even knew. And to quote my favorite recording artist Shea Diamond: I am America.” 

	Watch Mulvaney’s full video below.

schema.headline: Dylan Mulvaney Fires Back After Trump Mocks Her and Kaitlan Collins in White House Correspondents’ Dinner Speech: ‘Actually the Greatest Compliment of All’

title: ‘The Traitors’ India Sets August Season 2 Bow on Prime Video (EXCLUSIVE)
description: Prime Video will globally premiere Season 2 of “The Traitors,” its Indian adaptation of the hit international reality format in August, with new epi
body:
Prime Video will globally premiere Season 2 of “The Traitors,” its Indian adaptation of the hit international reality format in August, with new episodes streaming every Thursday.

	Karan Johar returns to host the season, in which 21 celebrities from various fields will compete in a game built around trust, betrayal and deception. The series is produced by Dharmatic Entertainment, Dharma Productions’ digital content studio, in collaboration with All3Media International, which oversees the Indian version of the BAFTA and Emmy-winning format created by IDTV. “The Traitors” has now been adapted in more than 40 territories worldwide.
	

	“The response to the first season of ‘The Traitors’ exceeded all expectations – it didn’t just entertain; it became a cultural moment,” said Nikhil Madhok, director and head of originals, Prime Video India. “‘The Traitors’ has become one of Prime Video India’s most defining reality franchises, transforming the genre with its unique blend of intelligent gameplay, psychological strategy, and riveting entertainment.”


	Madhok added that the new season raises the stakes with sharper gameplay and a new line-up of players.

	“The Indian adaptation of ‘The Traitors’ struck a powerful chord with viewers in its very first season, and we couldn’t be more delighted to see it return for another thrilling chapter,” added Sabrina Duguet, executive VP, APAC, All3Media International.

	Dharmatic Entertainment, in a statement, said the first season “ignited a nationwide obsession” and that the new run aims to stay true to the show’s “raw, unpredictable, and psychologically gripping essence.”
	

	Season 2 premieres Aug. 13.

	Formed in 2018, Dharmatic Entertainment has produced more than 25 titles, including “Call Me Bae” and “Love Storiyaan.” “The Traitors” is among its upcoming slate alongside a global game show format also hosted by Johar.

	All3Media International, which distributes programming to more than 1,000 broadcasters and platforms worldwide, has licensed “The Traitors” format to more than 30 territories for local versions, while episodes have aired via tape sales in more than 50 others. The distributor’s catalogue spans more than 35,000 hours of content, including scripted series such as “Liar” and “The Assassin,” alongside unscripted formats including “Race Across the World” and “Cash Cab.” All3Media recently completed a $8 billion merger with Banijay Entertainment.

	Prime Video’s Indian slate also includes “Mirzapur,” “The Family Man,” “Panchayat,” “Paatal Lok” and “Rise & Fall,” among other Originals.

schema.headline: ‘The Traitors’ India Sets August Season 2 Bow on Prime Video (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Nicola Coughlan, Paapa Essiedu and More Join Celebrity Auction to Raise Money for Students in Gaza
description: “Bridgerton” star Nicola Coughlan and “Harry Potter” series actor Paapa Essiedu are among more than 20 celebrities who are auctioning off meaningful
body:
“Bridgerton” star Nicola Coughlan and “Harry Potter” series actor Paapa Essiedu are among more than 20 celebrities who are auctioning off meaningful items to raise money for students in Gaza.

	The auction, coordinated by charity Phoenix Space, will begin on July 27 and also features items from Brian Cox, Gary Lineker, Paloma Faith, Maxine Peake, Juliet Stevenson, Charlotte Church, Harriet Walter, Vanessa Redgrave and Janet Suzman. It was spurred by the U.K. government’s announcement that it will help students in Gaza travel to and study in the U.K., but they must have fully-funded scholarships.
	

	Coughlan and her “Derry Girls” co-star Siobhán McSweeney have donated a signed behind-the-scenes photo, while Essiedu is auctioning his own personal “Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone” book. “I can’t imagine almost all universities being destroyed and the immense talent in every discipline wasted: no opportunities and no choice at all,” he said in a statement. “What a beautiful thing if this book in some way can unlock the futures of these brilliant students, too.”


	Other donated items include a signed Japan football shirt from Lineker; an “I Swear” production hoodie from Peake; the first poetry book Stevenson ever owned; a spot in Church’s next wellness retreat; Walter’s personal script from Donmar Warehouse’s all-female production of “Julius Caesar” and a signed copy of her book; a necklace Redgrave wore in the play “Long Day’s Journey Into Night”; and a vintage Christian Lacroix brooch from Suzman.

	According to Phoenix Space, hundreds of students in Gaza have been offered places at U.K. universities but do not have the funding to attend. This year, the students have offers from University College London, Imperial and Edinburgh in subjects like artificial intelligence and cognitive neuroscience.
	

	Bidding begins July 27 and will run for 10 days on the Scholarships for Gaza auction website.

schema.headline: Nicola Coughlan, Paapa Essiedu and More Join Celebrity Auction to Raise Money for Students in Gaza

title: Korea Box Office: Na Hong-Jin’s ‘Hope’ Holds Firm at No. 1 as Market Slows
description:
Science-fiction thriller “Hope” maintained its powerful grip on the top spot at the South Korean box office during the weekend of Jul. 24–26. 

	Acc
body:
Science-fiction thriller “Hope” maintained its powerful grip on the top spot at the South Korean box office during the weekend of Jul. 24–26. 

	According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the big-budget film generated $5.5 million from 767,366 admissions over the three-day window, securing a commanding 66.8% share of total market revenue.


	Directed by Na Hong-Jin, the film features an ensemble cast led by Hwang Jung-min, Zo In-sung, Jung Ho-yeon, Michael Fassbender, and Alicia Vikander. The narrative chronicles the desperate struggle for survival in a secluded harbor town after residents discover a mysterious alien entity on their outskirts. Following its record-setting opening frame, the local tentpole has now accumulated a gross of $25.3 million from 3,415,707 total viewers.
	

	“Minions & Monsters” was in second place, pulling in $793,103 from 117,916 admissions over the weekend. The film has lifted its cumulative total to $3.9 million from 562,965 total ticket buyers since its Jul. 15 debut.


	Disney’s live-action musical adaptation “Moana” took third place in its third weekend of release, collecting $593,187 from 87,033 admissions. The Pacific island adventure has reached an overall haul of $6.6 million from 909,270 admissions.

	“Toy Story 5” took fourth place, bringing in $376,522 from 53,975 ticket buyers. The animation is now nearing the $20 million mark in South Korea, boasting a local cumulative total of $19.8 million from 2,837,123 viewers since its mid-June launch.

	Faith-based animated production “David” claimed fifth place, adding $302,409 from 46,493 admissions over the frame. The biblical story of the shepherd boy turned king has pushed its local cume to $1.4 million from 220,351 viewers.
	

	Local psychological thriller “The Eyes” placed sixth, generating $269,004 from 37,141 admissions. Directed by Yeom Ji-ho and starring Shin Min-ah and Kim Nam-hee, the Korean remake of the Spanish thriller “Julia’s Eyes” has a gross of $10.6 million from 1,511,619 ticket buyers.

	Japanese anime feature “Dream Animals The Movie” debuted in seventh place, drawing $92,720 from 15,300 admissions over its opening weekend. Directed by Hitoshi Takekiyo and based on Ginbis’s popular long-selling animal biscuit brand, the animated adventure follows the colorful biscuit characters on a fantasy journey. Including previews, the title has earned $148,892 from 24,404 viewers.

	Josh Safdie’s table tennis comedy-drama “Marty Supreme,” starring Timothée Chalamet and Gwyneth Paltrow, took eighth place with a weekend gross of $37,623, bringing its total local cume to $923,581.

	Showbox’s action-horror hit “Colony,” directed by Yeon Sang-ho and starring Jun Ji-hyun, Koo Kyo-hwan, and Ji Chang-wook, took ninth place with $27,867, lifting its lifetime haul to $42.6 million from 5,949,979 total admissions since its May 21 rollout.

	Rounding out the top 10 was thehorror feature “Hokum,” which opened to $22,398 from 3,322 admissions over the frame. Since its Jul. 22 launch, the film has collected $50,203 from 7,972 viewers.

	The overall market collective gross for the weekend was $8.2 million, plummeting from last week’s $17.1 million.

schema.headline: Korea Box Office: Na Hong-Jin’s ‘Hope’ Holds Firm at No. 1 as Market Slows

title: John Oliver Returns to Expose Trump Family’s Shady Crypto Dealings: ‘We Badly Need Proper Guardrails’
description:
On Sunday night, John Oliver returned to the desk of “Last Week Tonight” from his summer hiatus, and there was, naturally, plenty to discuss.

	The
body:
On Sunday night, John Oliver returned to the desk of “Last Week Tonight” from his summer hiatus, and there was, naturally, plenty to discuss.

	The HBO host, whose contract is up at the end of 2026 — and whose parent company is facing a probable acquisition by Paramount Skydance, putting the lefty comedian directly in the crosshairs of a pro-Trump owner who’s already implemented a number of administration-friendly changes to CBS News — focused nearly the entirety of the show on President Trump, who’d previously called crypto “a disaster waiting to happen” that “may be fake” on Fox Business, but now refers to himself as “the first crypto president.”
	

	“Trump realized just how much money he personally could end up making from dealing with a speculative asset because it’s turned out to be a lot,” Oliver said. “His recent financial filings show that in just his first year back in office, his personal income surged to more than $2.2 billion, most of which came from his family’s crypto businesses, which brought in about $1.4 billion. In fact, crypto has become the family’s dominant business interest, overshadowing their real estate empire and every other business they have ever had.”


	As Virginia Canter, a prominent ethics attorney, stated, “This is like a perfect vehicle to funnel money to [Trump] and his family to enrich them.”

	Oliver then broke down two of the Trump family’s main crypto ventures: his meme coins (or jokes converted into crypto that purely have novelty value) and World Liberty Financial.

	“Most meme coins, seemingly by design, basically follow the trajectory of pump-and-dump schemes. They spike in value when they first come out and then immediately crash with insiders selling at the peak,” explained Oliver.
	

	You see, Trump and Melania launched meme coins just prior to his second inauguration, which skyrocketed in value and then plummeted. By the following December, Trump’s meme coin was down 92% in value while Melania’s was down 99%, but Trump walked away with $636 million. Trump even went as far as hosting an intimate private dinner for the 220 top holders of the Trump meme coin, thus offering “access to the White House in exchange for an investment in one of [Trump’s] crypto ventures,” reported The New York Times. Meanwhile, nearly 1 million people lost money in the Trump meme coin with their losses totaling $3.8 billion, according to the Times.

	“But Trump’s meme coin is just the tip of the iceberg here,” said Oliver, before segueing to the Trump family’s biggest crypto venture, World Liberty Financial.

	One way you can buy into World Liberty Financial is by purchasing a governance token, $WLFI, which merely allows you to vote on how the token is run, with 75% of purchases flowing to the company as a fee. And a number of sketchy deals have ensued involving World Liberty Financial. For one, Justin Sun invested $45 million in World Liberty Financial and then the SEC settled a fraud case being brought against him for $10 million with no wrongdoing admitted.

	If that weren’t enough, an Emirati investment fund pledged to invest $2 billion in World Liberty Financial. At minimum, Trump’s company netted $187 million from the deal. And two weeks later, Trump traveled to the UAE and announced they’d be able to buy hundreds of thousands of advanced AI chips from Nvidia (whereas the Biden administration had issued restrictions on the export of advanced AI chips to the UAE over security concerns).

	“It sure seems like Trump is exploiting crypto sketchiness for maximum profit,” declared Oliver.

	Trump is now pushing the CLARITY Act, which will shift crypto regulation from the SEC to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, a small federal agency with little to no enforcement power. 

	“If these conflicts of interest were as easy to understand as Jimmy Carter and his peanut farm I think there would be a lot more alarm about just how flagrantly corrupt and compromised Trump looks here,” Oliver maintained. “That is why we badly need proper guardrails going forward.”

schema.headline: John Oliver Returns to Expose Trump Family’s Shady Crypto Dealings: ‘We Badly Need Proper Guardrails’

title: China Box Office: ‘All Wishes Come True!’ Surges to Top Spot, Pushing ‘Kung Fu Soccer’ to Second
description: Pearl Studio’s animated fantasy feature “All Wishes Come True!” took over the top position at the mainland China box office during the July 24–26 we
body:
Pearl Studio’s animated fantasy feature “All Wishes Come True!” took over the top position at the mainland China box office during the July 24–26 weekend, generating RMB314.8 million ($46.3 million) in its second weekend of release. 

	Directed by Mu Zhengyang, the film now has a cumulative total of $112.5 million. The family-friendly mythological comedy centers on eight ordinary mortals who must combine their wit and courage to outsmart formidable deities, earning the legendary status of the Eight Immortals.
	

	Shenzhen Film Studio’s sports comedy “Kung Fu Soccer” moved to second place in its third weekend, adding $33.9 million. Directed by Stephen Chow, the hit production has reached a cumulative box office total of $286.6 million. The film follows an amateur women’s team as they integrate high-flying martial arts into professional soccer to contend for a major championship.


	Damai Entertainment’s sci-fi epic “The Decisive Moment” debuted in third position, bringing in $6.4 million over the weekend. Including early screenings since its July 25 launch, the film has taken $8.6 million to date. Directed by Zhang Disha from a script co-written with Hu Xiaoxi, and produced by industry veteran Huang Jianxin, the high-concept project previously served as the closing film of the Shanghai International Film Festival. Set across dual timelines, the narrative stars Huang Bo, Gao Ye, and Sun Yang as a trio of 2035 Chinese astronauts lost in space during a return mission, whose only lifeline is a mysterious encrypted signal linked back to a 1970 aerospace researcher played by Wu Lei.
	

	Universal’s “Obsession” opened in fourth place, collecting $4.9 million in its weekend debut. 

	Enlight Pictures’ youth drama “A Part of Me” rounded out the top five, pulling in $2.7 million in its second week of release. Directed by Ma Yingxin and starring Zhang Ruonan and Jolin Jin, the contemporary feature has accumulated $21.6 million as it tracks the emotional journey of a friendship spanning two decades.

	Mainland China’s overall weekend grosses reached $102.3 million, while the 2026 year-to-date revenue stands at $3.15 billion, down 33.6% from the same period in 2025.

title: D4vd Apple Music Account Hacked, Fake Song Posted Amid Preliminary Hearing
description:
D4vd
                          Apple Music Profile Hacked, Fake 'I Did It' Track Posted
body:
D4vd
                          Apple Music Profile Hacked, Fake 'I Did It' Track Posted
                          While Singer Remains Behind Bars
                      
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Amid singer D4vd being locked up and currently fighting to keep his murder case from going to trial, his Apple Music page has been hacked ... posting a fake song with a voice sounding like the jailed artist professing his love for the victim Celeste Rivas.
      
    
            The falsified track, titled "I DID IT" surfaced over the weekend, despite David Anthony Burke -- the artist known as D4vd -- remaining behind bars, without access to upload music himself. The track's artwork also features an aerial photo of D4vd's Tesla in the L.A. tow yard where Celeste's dismembered body was discovered last year.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The chorus repeatedly names Celeste ... describing her as "the girl with my name tattooed on her chest" and claiming her scent remains on his clothes "like cigarettes." The voice, mimicking D4vd's voice, also sings about hearing Celeste whenever he breathes ... missing her and fearing she will only love him after he dies.
      

            The timing couldn't be more jarring as Burke remains jailed without bail as his preliminary hearing unfolds in Los Angeles ... detailing the gruesome evidence prosecutors have against the singer.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As TMZ has reported ... prosecutors spent the past week laying out evidence they claim connects D4vd to Celeste's killing, including messages revealing tension between the pair shortly before her death. The court also heard D4vd had "Celeste" tattooed on one of his fingers, while prosecutors say Celeste had his name inked on hers.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            D4vd has pleaded not guilty to murder, continuous sexual abuse of a child under 14 and unlawful mutilation of human remains. The preliminary hearing will continue this week.
      
    
            We've reached out to Apple Music and Burke's camp ... so far, no word back.
      
      
              
          
                          
                Celeste Rivas
              
                          
                D4vd
